lesson.title: Applying a Value to Your Question
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: You have a real question. Today: practice genuinely applying a Sikhi value to it, not just naming the value in passing.

Genuinely applying a value means using it to actually think through your question, not just mentioning it. For example, applying Seva to a question about community responsibility might mean asking: does genuine Seva require personal sacrifice, or can it coexist with pursuing your own goals? What would 'selfless' actually look like in this specific situation? This kind of real thinking-through is different from just writing 'Seva teaches us to help others' as a surface-level mention. Choose one value from your Day 1 toolkit that connects to your Day 3 question, and write at least three real sentences genuinely thinking through how that value applies — not just defining the value.

You've now practiced the genuine analytical move your whole capstone project depends on: using a value to actually think, not just decorate an answer with it. Tomorrow we'll review this week and draft a complete capstone proposal.

objectives: Distinguish genuinely applying a value (using it to think) from merely mentioning it
Write a real, multi-sentence application of one value to the student's own capstone question
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review Day 1's toolkit and Day 3's question.
2. Introduce the difference between genuinely applying a value and merely mentioning it, using the Seva example.
3. Have the child choose one value and write a real application to their own question.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review and capstone proposal draft.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a sentence starter ('Applying [value] to my question means asking whether...') to get the genuine thinking started
Ready for more: ask them to also identify a second value from their toolkit that might apply differently, or even in tension with the first
This is the actual analytical skill the whole capstone project depends on — worth real time and care, not a rushed pass
teacherGuide.answerKey: A complete answer genuinely thinks through how a chosen value applies to the student's own question (at least three real sentences of analysis, not just a definition) — content varies by student, evaluated on whether it shows real thinking, not surface-level mention.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's capstone description, practicing the core analytical skill (genuinely applying a value, not just naming it) the year's whole project depends on.
